Archived.description: Its answer: the fragment, and whether it is archived now.

ChannelPage.description:
`GET /api/f/<name>/channels/<channel>?after=` (the channel's reader):
A page in ascending seq order. `next` is its last seq for a forward
read, its first seq for a backwards read, or the input cursor if empty.

ChannelRecord.description:
One record in a channel. Records are appended by the platform (`events`,
`ops`, and posts to a channel its fragment.json declares postable) or by
mutations' effects (app channels), never by a client's own hand.

body.description:
The JSON text the cell stored, passed through as it is: the cell
neither parses a body it just wrote nor one it reads back.

CodeStatus.description: The app code installed from the `live` pin.

error.description: Why the latest live commit's code was not installed, if it was not.

id.description:
What runs: `app:<hash>` (the live commit's `app.mjs` and `applib/`),
or `blessed:<template>@<release>` (the platform release's code, which
a fragment on a blessed template runs whatever its commit: decision 40).

sha.description: The live commit the code was installed from; `None` without app code.

Docked.description: Its answer: the fragment, and whether it is on their dock now.

Done.description:
`{ok: true}`: the call did what it asked, and there is nothing more to
say (a draft shown, say).

reason.description:
Why, where one status means several causes a person acts on
differently (billing's, seats' and orgs' refusals): the shell picks
its plain words by it. Add-only: absent from every other refusal, and
a client that knows none ignores it, and one that does not know this
one reads none (`reason_or_none`).

retry_after_ms.description:
How long to wait before asking again, in ms, where a refusal knows
(a 429 `rate_limited` of an embeddings model's rate limit: its
writer waits exactly this, then writes again). Add-only: absent
from every other refusal.

ErrorCode.description:
Every refusal the platform answers with, as `{"error": code, "message"}`.

Open (`x-fragment-open`, docs/wire): a code this reader does not know
is read by its HTTP status (the CLI's `Resp::refusal`), so one is added
without breaking a shipped client.

oneOf.description: 400: the request is malformed or breaks a rule.
401: no valid NIP-98 signature.
403: signed, but this principal may not do this.
404: no such fragment or route.
404: the fragment has no operation by that name.
404: the fragment's live commit has no `app.mjs`.
409: the fragment already exists.
409: this operation id was used with a different input.

409: a write's precondition no longer holds (a search source's
revision is not the one the write replaces).
413: a body, input, or result is over its limit.
422: the author's code refused or failed.
429: too many calls; retry later.
500: the platform failed.
502: code.storage (or another service the platform calls) failed.

503: the identity registry did not answer; nothing signed is
decided without it (docs/cloudflare-v1.md, R15, rule 7).

402: the paying person's ledger refused the spend (no credit, a
fragment's cap, a read-only overdraft; the message says which:
docs/ledger.md).

507: the app's database is at its cap (`limits::APP_DB_MAX_BYTES`);
the mutation was rolled back.

503: the app is answering as many calls at once as the runtime lets
it (a dynamic worker's concurrency limit); try again shortly.

503: the computer won't wake (its starts kept failing); its owner
can wake it to try again.

403: a computer's swap found no account to swap in: the agent's
owner has not connected that provider, or must connect it again.

500: the platform's object refuses its code's schema (fragment_core::
migrate): it holds a newer version (a rollback), another code's step,
or tables from before versions that need a reset. It answers nothing
else until newer code is deployed or an operator resets it; the
message names it and why.

503: a deploy is going out, and a call between the platform's own
Worker and one of its objects met another release on the other
side, which refused it before doing anything (docs/MODEL.md, "Calls
between releases"); try again in a few seconds.

FragmentKind.description:
What a fragment is to the people who use it (`fragment.json`'s `kind`,
decision 6): the shell lists each kind in its own place. An app unless
it says otherwise.

Open (`x-fragment-open`, docs/wire): a kind this build does not know
reads as `Other`.

oneOf.description:
A person's managed skills (decision 17: the blessed `skills`
template), which their agents' computers install.

A person's session archive (the blessed `sessions` template): the
conversations they had with an agent elsewhere, which `fragment
session import` brings in (templates/sessions/README.md).

A kind this build does not know: one a newer platform's list,
status or access view names (#587's), read as this so that one new
kind breaks no shipped CLI or pinned image. It is only ever read:
`parse` never answers it, so no `fragment.json` names it (the cell
refuses its install, as any kind it does not know), and it is
written only as `other`, a name no kind may take, never as a kind
it is not. Last: serde's `other` must be.

agentRole.description:
An agent fragment's role, as its face says it (`ListedFragment`'s
`agent_role`): what its runtime tells it it does.

blobMinBytes.description:
Files this large or larger are stored as blobs, their pointers in
git (absent from hosts without blobs: the TypeScript runtime).

inboxToken.description: Editors and up see the inbox token.

kind.description:
What it is, and its title, as its live `fragment.json` last said
(an app with no title until it has).

page.description:
What the page reported as its last preview card's shot loaded it
(docs/api.md, Cards); absent before the first.

reach.description:
It holds a secret or a door, so it is shared with no one but its
owner and their own agents (FIN-352, `Sharing::reach`): the share
sheet says so. Add-only: left out when false.

repo.description:
Its code.storage repo: `""` while not made yet (a chat's, made
after the create answers: docs/api.md, Names).

viewToken.description:
The share link's token: its owner's alone (and their agent's,
sharing for them, but on a connector), as the share sheet shows it. A member does not
share by link: they ask its owner.

IdentityKind.description:
What an identity is (docs/cloudflare-v1.md, R15). A fragment's own key
stays the fragment's and is not registered. An agent has a designated
owner, a person.

ListWatchFrame.description:
A frame of `GET /api/fragments/watch`, the socket that follows a
signer's list. Frames name nothing: on `changed` or `invited` the page
reads its list, or its invites, again with its own credential. The
cell writes these as constant text (cell/src/principal.rs).

Open (`x-fragment-open`, docs/wire): a reader ignores a frame it does
not know (the shell's list, the iOS app).

oneOf.description: First, as the socket opens.
Their list changed: a row added, gone, or changed.

The invites waiting on their emails changed: one made, renewed or
taken back.

ListedFragment.description:
A fragment the signer holds a role on: a row of `GET /api/fragments`
(and of a search's fragments), with the role they hold.

agentRole.description:
An agent fragment's role (its live `fragment.json`'s `meta.role`,
trimmed; none when it says nothing), as its last install said: the
tag the shell shows beside its name. Never any other fragment's.

agents.description:
Its agent members, the first added (a chat's lead) first, at most
`limits::LISTED_AGENTS_MAX`, as the fragment last said.

archived.description:
The signer archived it: their own view, not the fragment's (the
shell's sidebar leaves it out; search still finds it).

dock.description:
On the signer's dock: their own choice, not the fragment's (`PUT
/api/fragments/{name}/dock`), true until they take it off (the
shell's dock shows apps and brains, less these and the archived).
Left out while true, so a row from before the choice, or from an
older platform, reads as on it.

kind.description:
What it is, and its title, as its live `fragment.json` last said
(an app with no title until it has).

listed.description:
What its members are doing, as its channels that declare `listed`
last said (each member's newest such record, the newest first, at
most `limits::LISTED_POSTERS_MAX`): only those of channels this
row's role may read; none when there are none.

owned.description:
An agent's list `for` someone: whether that someone owns it (beside
the role the agent acts with there), as no name says any more.

picture.description:
Its picture, as the address on the platform that serves it: an
agent fragment's `avatar.png` at live (its agent's identity's
`/api/identities/<npub>/picture?v=…`), any other's icon
(`/api/f/<name>/icon?v=…`, docs/api.md, Icons).

pinned.description:
The signer pinned it: their own view, not the fragment's (`PUT
/api/fragments/{name}/pinned`; the shell's sidebar shows it first in
its section). Left out while false, so a row from an older platform
reads as not pinned.

preview.description:
A chat's newest message, its first line (at most
`limits::LISTED_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES`), as the signer's search holds it
(none when it holds none: docs/api.md, Search).

previewAt.description:
With `preview`: when its message was said (ms), so a list can put
its chats newest first.

sharing.description:
Its owner's row only: who else is in it, as the fragment last said
(`None` until it has).

unread.description:
A chat's messages the signer's search holds that came after the
last they saw (`PUT /api/fragments/{name}/seen`), at most
`limits::LISTED_UNREAD_MAX`; left out at 0.

ListedRecord.description:
A listed record as a person's list carries it (`ListedFragment.listed`):
a member's newest record of a kind its channel lists, sent to the lists
of the members whose role may read that channel, and to no one else's.

at.description:
When it was posted (ms); a poster who posts the same again moves it
at most `limits::LISTED_FRESH_MS` behind.

fields.description:
Its body's listed fields that are strings, each cut to
`limits::LISTED_VALUE_MAX_CHARS` characters.

principal.description: Who posted it: a member of the fragment.

LiveIn.description:
A frame a page sends. One that does not decode is answered with
`LiveOut::Error`, naming what was wrong.

oneOf.description:
One page of a channel's records from a cursor; the page that
reaches the end makes the socket live on the channel.

after.description: The records with `seq` after this one (0: from the start).

last.description: The channel's last this many records (at most `limits::CHANNEL_PAGE`).

oneOf.description:
Runs a query as the socket's principal and role; a `result` with the
same id answers it.

Shares `data` with everyone on the page (at most
`limits::PRESENCE_MAX_BYTES`); `null`, or no `data`, clears it. At
most `limits::PRESENCE_PER_S` a second, after a burst of
`limits::PRESENCE_BURST`: faster ones are dropped, each with an error.

LiveOut.description:
A frame the fragment sends.

Open (`x-fragment-open`, docs/wire): a reader skips a frame it does not
know (the CLI's `channel --follow`, cell/client.mjs, the iOS app).

oneOf.description:
First on every socket: who the page is to the fragment (the role is
fixed while the socket stays open), the platform's origin (the one
page that frames it with its person's session, whose messages a
framed page may take: docs/api.md, The shell), and everyone on the
page who shares presence.
A record of a channel: one of a page, or a new one while live.

After each page: the cursor past it, and whether more follow. With
`more`, the socket is not live on the channel yet: subscribe again
from `next`.

One socket's presence changed: its data, or `null` once it cleared
it or left.

A channel's draft: a record its poster is writing (a reply as it
streams), its whole text so far, or `null` once they stopped.
Never stored; the record that carries the same `turn` replaces it.
`thinking`: a job's text step whose model reasons with no words yet
(its text empty), for this many ms so far.
A mutation applied: re-run live queries.
A query's answer.

result.description: The query's answer, any JSON (`null` included), as the app gave it.

oneOf.description: A frame the fragment refused, and why; the socket stays open.

addedBy.description: Who granted it: the owner, or their agent for them (an invite's maker).

owner.description: An agent member's owner, who reads what it reads.

MessageHit.description:
One record whose text matched: where it is, when it was written, and
a snippet of its text around the match (plain text, at most
`limits::SEARCH_SNIPPET_MAX_BYTES`).

seq.description: The record's place in its channel.

description.description:
What it does, in plain text, for a person or an agent choosing it
(1 to `limits::OP_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS` characters). None when the
manifest gives none, and then absent from the wire.

ephemeral.description:
A mutation whose calls leave no ledger row (`"ephemeral": true`):
no replay (the same id runs again) and no effects (docs/api.md, Apps).

input.description: Its input's JSON Schema (the supported subset); also its tool schema.

role.description: The weakest role that may call it.

oneOf.description: Runs as a Workflow, one durable step at a time.

source.description: The script or resource it names (`url`, or `url:line:column`).

text.description:
What the page or the browser said (cut to
`fragment_core::card::ERROR_BYTES_MAX`, as `source` is).

oneOf.description: An uncaught exception or an unhandled rejection (a syntax error too).
`console.error`, or a `console.assert` that failed.
A load that failed: the page itself, a script, an image, a fetch.

A load the browser refused for its security: a Content Security
Policy violation, mixed content.

PageReport.description:
The errors a page reported as the platform loaded it for its preview
card, as a visitor without an account sees it: as it loaded and in
the second after, with no interaction.

dropped.description: How many more it reported past those.

errors.description: The first it reported, in order (at most `fragment_core::card::ERRORS_MAX`).

live.description: The live commit the shot loaded.

Pinned.description: Its answer: the fragment, and whether it is pinned now.

live.description: The commit installed as `live`; none before the first deploy.

main.description: The commit `main` points at; none before its first.

PostRecord.description:
`POST /api/f/<name>/channels/<channel>` (the channel's `post` role): a
record the platform appends as the poster. `id` is the poster's own
(`^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$`): the same id with the same body answers the
record it appended and appends nothing; with another body it is 409.

Posted.description: A post's answer: the record, and whether this id had posted it before.

Present.description: One socket's presence (`data` is never `null` in a `hello`).

PutDraft.description:
`PUT /api/f/<name>/channels/<channel>/draft`, by whoever may post
there: a record not written yet, as it is written (a reply as it
streams), shown to the channel's readers live and never stored (a
`draft` frame on `__live`); `text: null` stops it. The record its poster
then writes with the same `turn` replaces it on a page.

Reason.description: A refusal's cause, for the people who read it: billing's, seats', orgs' and reach's. Open: a reason a reader does not know reads as none.

Role.description:
A member's role in a fragment. `Public` is the floor anyone who can see
the fragment holds; the others are granted. Ordered weakest first.

SearchAnswer.description:
`GET /api/search?q=` (any signer): the signer's fragments whose title
or name match every word of the query, then the messages that do,
newest first, from the fragments they hold a role on now.

Seen.description:
`PUT /api/fragments/{name}/seen`'s answer: the signer has seen the
fragment's messages their search holds, so its row counts none unread.

unread.description: Always 0: none of its messages is unread now.

SetArchived.description:
`PUT /api/fragments/{name}/archived`: the signer's own view of a
fragment they hold a role on.

SetDock.description:
`PUT /api/fragments/{name}/dock`: the signer's own choice of whether
their dock shows a fragment they hold a role on.

SetPinned.description:
`PUT /api/fragments/{name}/pinned`: the signer's own choice of whether
a fragment they hold a role on is pinned in their sidebar.

Sharing.description:
A fragment's sharing, in its owner's list (the platform's page): who
may open it, how many members it has, how many of them are guests
(neither the owner nor an agent of theirs), and how many invites wait
on an email (`None` in a row sent before rows counted them).

reach.description:
It holds a secret or a door, so it is shared with no one but its
owner and their own agents (FIN-352: `Reason::PrivateWhileReaching`,
`Reason::UnshareFirst`). Add-only: left out when false, and a row
from before it reads none.

canonical.description: Its own origin, where its page is served.

platform.description:
The platform's own origin, where people open its join links and
send its inbox's webhooks: a client inside a computer reaches the
API at an internal host, so a link for a person names this one.

Visibility.description: Who can see a fragment: everyone, holders of its share link, or members.

frame.description: The session of a fragment's page framed by another page (docs/api.md, Frame sessions); `fragment_frame` over plain http.
frame.name: __Host-fragment_frame

link.description: A fragment's share link's token (docs/api.md, Sharing); its page keeps it in a cookie of its origin after.
link.name: view

nip98.description: NIP-98: `Authorization: Nostr <base64 event>`, a kind-27235 event signed over the method, the URL and the body's SHA-256 (crates/nip98).

session.description: The shell's session, from the platform's own page (docs/api.md, Sign-in); `fragment_session` over plain http.
session.name: __Host-fragment_session

site.description: A fragment's own page's session, on its origin (docs/api.md, Sign-in); `fragment_site` over plain http.
site.name: __Host-fragment_site

info.description: The routes clients call and the shapes they send and read, generated by `cargo xtask wire` from crates/proto (its routes.rs and the types it names). docs/api.md says what each route means, who may call it, and its limits; crates/proto/wire.lock is what may not change.

post.summary: Append a `message` record as the poster.

put.summary: Show a record as it is written to the channel's live readers; never stored.

get.summary: A fragment's members, the first added first.
A fragment's status, as the caller's role sees it.

parameters.description: An agent's: the identity it acts for. The rows are the fragments that identity holds a role on where the agent or its owner is a member, each with the role the agent acts with there, `owned` on that identity's own, and no `listed`.
parameters.name: for

get.summary: The signer's fragments, a row each.

put.summary: Archive or unarchive a fragment in the signer's own list.
Put a fragment on the signer's dock, or take it off.
Pin or unpin a fragment in the signer's sidebar.
The signer has seen a fragment's messages: its row counts none unread.

parameters.name: q
